nodes.name: Combinatorial property of Boolean functions
nodes.statement: A combinatorial property is a sequence $\{C_n \subseteq F_n\}_{n \in \omega}$, where $F_n$ is the set of all Boolean functions in $n$ variables; $f_n$ has property $C_n$ iff $f_n \in C_n$.

nodes.name: Natural combinatorial property
nodes.statement: A combinatorial property $C_n$ is natural if it contains a subset $C_n^* \subseteq C_n$ satisfying constructivity ($f_n \in C_n^*$ decidable in time polynomial in $|f_n| = 2^n$) and largeness ($|C_n^*| \geq 2^{-O(n)} \cdot |F_n|$).
conclusions: Constructivity: predicate $f_n \in C_n^*$ is in $\mathrm{P}$ (poly in $2^n$)

nodes.name: Property useful against $\mathrm{P/poly}$
nodes.statement: $C_n$ is useful against $\mathrm{P/poly}$ if for any sequence $f_1, f_2, \ldots$ with $f_n \in C_n$, the circuit size of $f_n$ is super-polynomial: for any constant $k$, eventually circuit-size$(f_n) > n^k$.

nodes.name: Natural proof against $\mathrm{P/poly}$
nodes.statement: A proof that some explicit function $\{g_n\}$ does not have polynomial-sized circuits is natural against $\mathrm{P/poly}$ if it (more or less explicitly) contains a definition of a natural combinatorial property $C_n$ that is useful against $\mathrm{P/poly}$.

nodes.name: $\Gamma$-natural property with density $\delta_n$
nodes.statement: For complexity classes $\Gamma, \Lambda$: $C_n$ is $\Gamma$-natural with density $\delta_n$ if it has $C_n^* \subseteq C_n$ with constructivity ($f_n \in C_n^*$ computable in $\Gamma$) and largeness $|C_n^*| \geq \delta_n \cdot |F_n|$.

nodes.name: Property useful against complexity class $\Lambda$
nodes.statement: $C_n$ is useful against $\Lambda$ if for any sequence $f_n$ where the event $f_n \in C_n$ happens infinitely often, $\{f_n\} \notin \Lambda$.

nodes.name: $\Gamma$-natural proof against $\Lambda$
nodes.statement: A lower bound proof that some explicit function is not in $\Lambda$ is $\Gamma$-natural against $\Lambda$ with density $\delta_n$ if it states a $\Gamma$-natural property $C_n$ which is useful against $\Lambda$ with density $\delta_n$. Default settings: $\Gamma = \mathrm{P}$, $\Lambda = \mathrm{P/poly}$, $\delta_n = 2^{-O(n)}$.

nodes.name: Hardness of pseudo-random generator
nodes.statement: For a pseudo-random generator $G_k : \{0,1\}^k \to \{0,1\}^{2k}$, its hardness $H(G_k)$ is the minimal $S$ such that there exists a circuit $C$ of size $S$ with $|P[C(G_k(x))=1] - P[C(y)=1]| \geq 1/S$, where $x \sim \{0,1\}^k$ and $y \sim \{0,1\}^{2k}$.

nodes.name: Half-exponential function
nodes.statement: An integer-valued $t(n)$ is half-exponential if it is nondecreasing and $t^{-1}(n^C) \leq o(\log t(n))$ for every $C > 0$. Roughly, the second iteration of $t$ should grow faster than the exponential.

nodes.name: Formal complexity measure
nodes.statement: A formal complexity measure is an integer-valued function $\mu$ on $F_n$ with $\mu(f) \leq 1$ for $f \in \{x_1,\ldots,x_n,\neg x_1,\ldots,\neg x_n\}$ and $\mu(f * g) \leq \mu(f) + \mu(g)$ for all $f,g \in F_n$ and $* \in \{\wedge, \vee\}$.

nodes.name: Hard-bit predicate $B_{p,g}$ of discrete logarithm
nodes.statement: For a prime $p$ and generator $g$ of $\mathbb{Z}_p^*$, $B_{p,g}(x) = 1$ iff $\log_g x \leq (p-1)/2$ (and $0$ otherwise). $B_{p,g}$ is a hard bit of the discrete logarithm.

nodes.name: No $\mathrm{P/poly}$-natural proof against $\mathrm{P/poly}$
nodes.statement: There is no lower bound proof which is $\mathrm{P/poly}$-natural against $\mathrm{P/poly}$, unless $H(G_k) \leq 2^{k^{o(1)}}$ for every pseudo-random generator $G_k : \{0,1\}^k \to \{0,1\}^{2k}$ in $\mathrm{P/poly}$. In particular, if $2^{n^\epsilon}$-hard functions exist, no $\mathrm{P/poly}$-natural proof exists against $\mathrm{P/poly}$.
conclusions: No $\mathrm{P/poly}$-natural lower bound proof against $\mathrm{P/poly}$ exists

nodes.name: Nisan's $\mathrm{AC}^0[2]$-secure pseudo-random generator
nodes.statement: For any integer $d$, there exists a family $G_{n,s} \in F_n$ ($s$ a seed of size polynomial in $n$) such that $G_{n,s} \in \mathrm{AC}^0[2]$ and for any depth-$d$ size-$2^{O(n)}$ circuit $C_n$: $|P[C_n(f_n)=1] - P[C_n(G_{n,s})=1]| < 2^{-\omega(n)}$.

nodes.name: No $\mathrm{AC}^0$-natural proof against $\mathrm{AC}^0[2]$
nodes.statement: There is no lower bound proof which is $\mathrm{AC}^0$-natural against $\mathrm{AC}^0[2]$.

nodes.name: No $\mathrm{P}^{\mathrm{qpoly}}$-natural proof against $\mathrm{P/poly}$
nodes.statement: There is no lower bound proof which is $\mathrm{P}^{\mathrm{qpoly}}$-natural against $\mathrm{P/poly}$ unless $H(G_k) \leq 2^{k^{o(1)}}$ for every pseudo-random generator $G_k : \{0,1\}^k \to \{0,1\}^{2k}$ in $\mathrm{P/poly}$. Here $\mathrm{P}^{\mathrm{qpoly}}$ is the class of nonuniform quasi-polynomial size circuits ($n^{\log^{O(1)} n}$).

nodes.name: No natural proof for discrete logarithm half-exponential bounds
nodes.statement: Let $t(n)$ be a half-exponential function. There is no combinatorial property $C_n$ useful against $\mathrm{SIZE}(t(n))$ satisfying $\mathrm{P/poly}$-constructivity and largeness such that $\bigcup_n C_n$ contains infinitely many functions of the form $B_{p,g}(x)$.
conclusions: $\bigcup_n C_n$ does not contain infinitely many $B_{p,g}$ functions

nodes.name: No natural proof of exponential bounds for discrete log
nodes.statement: There is no combinatorial property $C_n$ useful against $\bigcup_{\epsilon>0} \mathrm{SIZE}(2^{n^\epsilon})$ satisfying $\mathrm{P/poly}$-constructivity and largeness such that $\bigcup_n C_n$ contains infinitely many functions of the form $B_{p,g}(x)$.

nodes.name: Largeness for formal complexity measures (main)
nodes.statement: Let $\mu$ be a formal complexity measure on $F_n$ and $\mu(f) = t$ for some $f \in F_n$. Then (a) for at least $1/4$ of all $g \in F_n$, $\mu(g) \geq t/4$; (b) for any $\epsilon = \epsilon(n)$, for at least $(1-\epsilon)$ fraction of $g \in F_n$, $\mu(g) \geq \Omega(t/(n + \log(1/\epsilon))^2) - n$.

nodes.name: Boolean algebra representation theorem
nodes.statement: Let $B$ be a finite Boolean algebra with $N$ atoms and $S \subseteq B$. (a) If $|S| > (3/4)|B|$, every element of $B$ can be represented as $(s_1 \wedge s_2) \vee (s_3 \wedge s_4)$ with $s_i \in S$. (b) If $S$ contains all atoms and coatoms, every element can be represented as $\bigvee_{i=1}^{l} \bigwedge_{j=1}^{l} s_{ij}$, $s_{ij} \in S$, $l \leq O(\log(N \cdot |B|/|S|))$.

nodes.name: Atom-cover lemma
nodes.statement: Let $B$ be a finite Boolean algebra with $N$ atoms and $S \subseteq B$. There exists $S_0 \subseteq S$ of cardinality $O(\log N)$ such that $\bigwedge S_0$ contains at most $O(\log(|B|/|S|))$ atoms.

nodes.name: Sign-preserving integer rounding
nodes.statement: Let $a_1, \ldots, a_N \in \mathbb{R}$. There exist $a'_1, \ldots, a'_N \in \mathbb{Z}$ with $|a'_i| \leq \exp(O(N \log N))$ such that for every $x_i \in \{-1,1\}^N$, $\mathrm{sgn}(\sum_{i=1}^N a_i x_i) = \mathrm{sgn}(\sum_{i=1}^N a'_i x_i)$.

nodes.name: Schwartz–Zippel-style root bound
nodes.statement: Every integer polynomial $p(x_1, \ldots, x_n)$ of degree $d$ which is not identically zero on $\{-1,1\}^n$ differs from zero on at least $2^{n-d}$ points from $\{-1,1\}^n$.

nodes.name: Largeness of high-weak-degree property
nodes.statement: For a uniformly chosen $f_n \in F_n$, $P[d_w(f_n) \geq n/20] > 1 - 2^{-2^{\Omega(n)}}$, where $d_w$ is the weak degree (least $k$ such that some nonzero degree-$k$ polynomial weakly represents $f_n$).

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.1 (no $\mathrm{P/poly}$-natural proof against $\mathrm{P/poly}$)
nodes.statement: By contradiction. Use the Goldreich–Goldwasser–Micali construction to convert $G_k$ into a pseudo-random function generator $f$, then show $C_n$ provides a hybrid statistical test breaking $G_k$.

nodes.name: Assume $C_n^* = C_n$
nodes.statement: For contradiction suppose a $\mathrm{P/poly}$-natural proof exists with associated property $C_n$. WLOG assume $C_n^* = C_n$ (the constructive subset).

nodes.name: GGM-style pseudo-random function generator from $G_k$
nodes.statement: Set $n = \lceil k^\epsilon \rceil$. Using $G = (G_0, G_1) : \{0,1\}^k \to \{0,1\}^k \times \{0,1\}^k$, define $G_y = G_{y_n} \circ G_{y_{n-1}} \circ \cdots \circ G_{y_1}$ and $f(x)(y) = $ first bit of $G_y(x)$.

nodes.name: $f(x) \notin C_n$ from usefulness
nodes.statement: Since $f(x)(y)$ is computable by poly-size circuits, by usefulness $f(x) \notin C_n$ for any fixed $x$ and large $k$. Hence $C_n \cap \{f(x) | x \in \{0,1\}^k\} = \emptyset$.

nodes.name: Statistical test for $f(x)$
nodes.statement: Largeness gives $P[C_n(f_n) = 1] \geq 2^{-O(n)}$ for random $f_n$, while $P[C_n(f(x)) = 1] = 0$. Therefore $|P[C_n(f_n)=1] - P[C_n(f(x))=1]| \geq 2^{-O(n)}$, computable by size $2^{O(n)}$ circuits.

nodes.name: Hybrid argument over binary tree
nodes.statement: Arrange internal nodes of binary tree of height $n$ as $v_1, \ldots, v_{2^n - 1}$ (sons before parents). The hybrid $f_{i,n}$ interpolates between $f_n$ ($i = 0$) and $f(x)$ ($i = 2^n - 1$); some adjacent pair has distinguishing advantage $2^{-O(n)}$.

nodes.name: Statistical test for $G$ and conclusion
nodes.statement: Fix all $x_v$ except $v_{i+1}$ to preserve the bias; this yields a circuit-size-$2^{O(n)}$ test distinguishing $G(x_{v_{i+1}})$ from a random pair, so $H(G_k) \leq 2^{O(n)} = 2^{O(k^\epsilon)}$. Since $\epsilon$ was arbitrary, $H(G_k) \leq 2^{k^{o(1)}}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.3 (no $\mathrm{AC}^0$-natural proof against $\mathrm{AC}^0[2]$)
nodes.statement: Assume the contrary; let $d$ bound the depth of the size-$2^{O(n)}$ circuit computing $C_n$. Apply Theorem 4.2's pseudo-random generator $G_{n,s}$ in $\mathrm{AC}^0[2]$: usefulness gives $C_n(G_{n,s}) = 0$ but largeness contradicts $|P[C_n(f_n)=1] - P[C_n(G_{n,s})=1]| < 2^{-\omega(n)}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.1 from Theorem 5.2
nodes.statement: Set $S = \{g | \mu(g) < t/4\}$ for (a) and $S = \{g | \mu(g) < \delta t/(n + \log(1/\epsilon))^2\}$ for (b). If $|S|$ exceeded the threshold, Theorem 5.2 would represent $f$ in form (9) or (10), and subadditivity of $\mu$ would give $\mu(f) < t$, contradiction.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.2(a)
nodes.statement: Fix $b_0 \in B$. Use the representation $b_0 = (\mathbf{b} \wedge (\neg\mathbf{b} \vee b_0)) \vee (\neg\mathbf{b} \wedge (\mathbf{b} \vee b_0))$ with random $\mathbf{b}$. All four random variables are uniform on $B$, and $|S| > (3/4)|B|$ implies all four lie in $S$ for some choice.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.2(b)
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 5.3 twice: first to express good $c \in B_0$ as $\bigvee s_j$ via $S \cap B(c)$, then dually to express $b_0 = \bigwedge c_i$ via good elements. This yields the OR-of-AND representation with $l \leq O(\log(N|B|/|S|))$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.3 (atom-cover)
nodes.statement: Call atom $a$ good if $P[a \leq s] \geq 2/3$ (random $s \in S$), else bad. Standard entropy counting bounds bad atoms by $O(\log(|B|/|S|))$. A random $S_0 \subseteq S$ of size $C \log N$ has, for each good atom, $P[a \leq \bigwedge S_0] < N^{-1}$, so some $S_0$ has $\bigwedge S_0$ contain only bad atoms.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.1 (largeness of weak-degree)
nodes.statement: If $f_n$ is weakly represented by polynomial $p$ of degree $\leq n/20$, apply Proposition 3.2 to coefficients to bound bit-size by $2^{n(2 H(1/20)+o(1))}$. Then $f_n$ is recoverable from $(p', f'_n)$ where $f'_n$ are the values on zeros of $p'$, of total bit-size $< 2^n$. Counting argument completes the proof since $2 H(1/20) < 19/20$.

nodes.name: $\mathrm{P}$ vs $\mathrm{NP}$ (circuit-complexity formulation)
nodes.statement: Prove a nonuniform separation: that $\mathrm{SAT}$ (or some other problem in $\mathrm{NP}$) does not have polynomial-size circuits, i.e., $\mathrm{NP} \not\subseteq \mathrm{P/poly}$.

nodes.name: Discrete logarithm problem
nodes.statement: Given prime $p$, generator $g$ of $\mathbb{Z}_p^*$, and $y \in \mathbb{Z}_p^*$, compute $\log_g y$. Worst-case and average-case hardness coincide.

nodes.name: $\mathrm{AC}^0$-natural parity lower bound (Furst–Saxe–Sipser, Yao, Håstad)
nodes.statement: $C_n(f_n) = 1$ iff no restriction with the appropriate number of unassigned variables forces $f_n$ to a constant. The proof shows usefulness against $\mathrm{AC}^0$ via the switching lemma; $C_n^* = C_n$ is large by counting and is in $\mathrm{AC}^0$ (depth-3, polynomial-sized in $2^n$). Used to derive $\mathrm{PARITY} \notin \mathrm{AC}^0$.

nodes.name: Smolensky's $\mathrm{NC}^2$-natural $\mathrm{AC}^0[3]$ lower bound for parity
nodes.statement: $C_n^*(f_n) = 1$ iff $\dim(f_n L + L) \geq N(1/2 + \epsilon)$ where $L$ is the space of polynomials over $\mathbb{Z}_3$ of degree $< n/2$. Computing rank is in $\mathrm{NC}^2$; largeness from $C_n^*(f_n)=1$ or $C_n^*(x_1 \cdots x_n - f_n)=1$. Useful against $\mathrm{AC}^0[3]$.

nodes.name: Aspnes–Beigel–Furst–Rudich perceptron lower bound
nodes.statement: $C_n^*(f_n) = 1$ iff weak degree $d_w(f_n) >$ threshold; usefulness against constant-depth circuits with one majority gate; constructivity via linear programming ($\mathrm{P}$-natural); largeness from Theorem 3.1.

nodes.name: Håstad shrinkage formula-size lower bound
nodes.statement: Andreev's function $A_{2n}$ on bits $a_1,\ldots,a_n; b_1,\ldots,b_n$ has formula complexity $\geq \Omega(n^3)$. The natural property $C_{2n}^*$: there is a restriction of $b$'s such that random restrictions of $a$'s shrink the formula to $\Omega(n/\log n)$. $\mathrm{AC}^0$-constructive (only $2^{O(n)}$ small formulas).

nodes.name: Hajnal–Maass–Pudlák–Szegedy–Turán depth-2 threshold lower bound
nodes.statement: $C_n^*$: function viewed as a Boolean matrix is almost Hadamard (small dot products of rows/columns). Constructive in $\mathrm{TC}^0$ via dot-product threshold gates. Useful against depth-2 threshold circuits.

nodes.name: Razborov switching-and-rectifier network lower bound
nodes.statement: $C_n^*$: function admits the property $A_{\log\log n}$ after restriction to $n/2$ zeros, extended by a further $n/2 - \log\log n$ zeros. $\mathrm{AC}^0$-constructive; largeness via $n^{3/2}$ near-disjoint extensions. Yields $\Omega(n \alpha(n))$ network-size lower bound for symmetric Booleans.

nodes.name: Counting / diagonalization arguments are not natural
nodes.statement: Traditional counting/diagonalization arguments yield $C_n$ defined by '$f_n$ is hard,' which has no obvious large constructive subset. Theorem 4.1 implies under the PRG assumption no such $C_n^*$ exists, so counting arguments are presumably not natural.

nodes.name: Monotone lower bounds escape the framework
nodes.statement: Strong lower bounds against monotone circuit models (refs [24,17,26–28,37]) lie outside the framework: properties used are feasible, but no good analogue of largeness exists since 'random monotone function' is not well-defined.

nodes.name: Naturalization extends to Turing-reducible families
nodes.statement: The proof of Theorem 4.5 extends to any collection $\{f_{p,g}\}$ poly-time nonuniformly Turing reducible to the corresponding discrete logarithm problem in place of $\{B_{p,g}\}$.

nodes.name: Duality interpretation in Conclusion
nodes.statement: Any natural proof against complexity class $\Lambda$ implicitly shows $\Lambda$ does not contain strong pseudo-random function generators, giving an algorithm to break any such generator. Working on lower bounds via natural methods is like breaking a code determined by the class one is working against.
